To enable automated evaluation, models were constrained to output a structured JSON array. Each
array contains objects with two fields:
• span: The exact text substring containing a hallucination (null if none).
• type: One of Contradiction, Unconfirmed, Excess, Partial, Missing, Oversight (null if no hallucin-
ation).
This format ensures consistent parsing and metric computation across all baselines.
8 Results
Tables 2, 3 and 4 present evaluation results across the three subtasks: binary hallucination detection,
multi-label type classification, and span identification. Results are sorted by the accuracy metric. All
precision, recall, F1-score and Jaccard metrics are macro-averaged 22.
8.1 Overall Performance
Binary hallucination detection. Gemini-2.5-Pro achieves the highest binary performance (accur-
acy 81.3, F1 78.5) with perfect format compliance, followed by Gemini-2.5-Flash (accuracy 75.2, F1
72.2). The proprietary GPT5.1-Pro achieves near-perfect format adherence (99.4% SR) with accuracy of
69.5. Y andexGPT-5.1 shows moderate performance (accuracy 54.3) with acceptable format compliance
(73.5% SR).
Open-source models show significant variation: T-pro-it-2.0 and gpt-oss-20b demonstrate reasonable
detection (accuracy 65.0 and 63.0, respectively) but lower success rates (81.9 for both). GLM-4.6v
demonstrates competitive detection capability (accuracy 70.1) despite moderate success rate (89.5). The
reasoning-focused Kimi-k2-thinking achieves 56.4% accuracy with notably high precision (57.6) but low
recall (31.8) and reduced format compliance (63.9% SR).
Larger models exhibit divergent behavior: Llama-3.3-70B and Qwen3-235B attain perfect format ad-
herence but substantially weaker detection accuracy (41.6 and 35.5, respectively), though both maintain
high recall (54.6 and 50.9). DeepSeek-chat-v3-0324 underperforms on accuracy (37.0) with moder-
ate format compliance (79.7% SR). Small

Multi-label type classification. Gemini-2.5-Pro dominates multi-label classification (exact match ac-
curacy 71.6, macro F1 47.0, Jaccard 34.1) with minimal Hamming Loss (7.0), confirming superior per-
label prediction quality. Gemini-2.5-Flash follows at a distance (accuracy 63.1, F1 31.7, Jaccard 21.9).
GLM-4.6v model achieves competitive accuracy (61.7) with strong precision (40.7), closely match-
ing the Flash variant. Among the remaining top-tier models, T-pro-it-2.0, gpt-oss-20b, GPT5.1-Pro,
Y andexGPT-5.1, and Kimi-k2-thinking cluster in the 51.9–58.1% accuracy range, though with varying
precision-recall trade-offs: T-pro-it-2.0 and gpt-oss-20b favor precision (38.8 and 41.9), while Kimi
shows the highest precision (48.7) but lowest recall (21.2) in this group.
A performance gap emerges below 20% accuracy: DeepSeek-chat-v3-0324, Llama-3.3-70B, and
Qwen3-235B achieve accuracies of 17.3%, 16.1%, and 11.4% respectively, with DeepSeek and Qwen
showing relatively higher recall (33.7 and 34.8). Smaller models (Gemma-3-27b-it, Y andexGPT-5-8B-
Lite, Qwen3-8B, T-lite-it-2.1) achieve accuracies below 7%, indicating severe difficulty with fine-grained
type discrimination. Overall low Jaccard scores (3.8–34.1) across all models reflect the inherent difficulty
of multi-label hallucination type classification.
Span identification. Gemini-2.5-Pro achieves the highest span accuracy (71.7), Jaccard (73.6), and
ROUGE-L (79.4), establishing a clear performance ceiling. The next tier—comprising gpt-oss-20b,
T-pro-it-2.0, GLM-4.6v, Kimi-k2-thinking, and Y andexGPT-5.1—delivers competitive span extraction
with accuracies between 63.8 and 67.7% and ROUGE-L scores ranging from 65.2 to 72.2. Notably,
Gemini-2.5-Flash drops to seventh place (accuracy 61.9, ROUGE-L 70.7), suggesting that span extrac-
tion benefits less from the Flash optimization compared to classification tasks. GPT5.1-Pro shows mod

patterns observed across top models: Gemini-2.5-Flash drops from 79.8% to 66.4%, GLM-4.6v from
76.8% to 57.4%, and GPT5.1-Pro from 73.4% to 62.0%.
The difficulty gap is even more pronounced for multi-label classification: Gemini-2.5-Pro shows a 21.2
percentage point drop (78.9% to 57.7%), while Gemini-2.5-Flash drops 28.7 points (73.0% to 44.3%).
This pattern holds across most models, with SberQuAD multi-label accuracies consistently 20–35 per-
centage points higher than ruSciBench. The only exceptions are models already performing poorly on
both datasets (below 30% accuracy).
Span identification shows the largest complexity gap: Gemini-2.5-Pro drops 22.3 points (79.4% to
57.1%), Gemini-2.5-Flash drops 29.9 points (72.2% to 42.3%), and gpt-oss-20b drops 27.2 points (77.1%
to 49.9%). This validates our perturbation strategy and highlights the added challenge of scientific ter-
minology, domain-specific reasoning, and precise boundary identification in specialized contexts.
Notably, some models show extreme asymmetry: Kimi-k2-thinking achieves 76.0% on SberQuAD
binary detection but only 19.1% on ruSciBench—a 56.9 point gap, the largest observed. This suggests
certain models may overfit to general knowledge patterns and fail to transfer reasoning capabilities to
scientific domains.
Model consistency. Top-performing models (Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-2.5-Flash, GLM-4.6v) main-
tain consistent ranking across all task-dataset combinations. The middle tier (T-pro-it-2.0, gpt-oss-20b,
